notes: EBIT is operationalized as GAAP Operating Income from Delta’s Consolidated Statements of Operations (i.e., excludes non-operating items like interest and investment gains/losses). ([s2.q4cdn.com](https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/DAL-12-31-2025-10K-2-10-26-Filed.pdf))

Capex is operationalized as the sum of Flight equipment additions and Ground property/technology additions from the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows (absolute magnitudes). ([s2.q4cdn.com](https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/DAL-12-31-2025-10K-2-10-26-Filed.pdf))

NWC construction: NWC = (Total current assets − cash and cash equivalents − short-term investments, if present) − (Total current liabilities − current maturities of debt and finance leases). This yields negative NWC for DAL due to large current liabilities (including air traffic liability and deferred revenue). ([s2.q4cdn.com](https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/DAL-12-31-2025-10K-2-10-26-Filed.pdf))

WACC is computed using CAPM cost of equity (risk-free + beta * implied ERP) and an after-tax cost of debt derived from 2025 interest expense net divided by total debt; weights use market value of equity from the finance snapshot and book total debt for weighting. ([finance.yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/DAL//?utm_source=openai))

Investments is set to equity investments on the balance sheet (equity investments line item) as the closest available non-operating investment adjustment input in the schema; if your DCF pipeline uses a different investments definition, adjust accordingly. ([s2.q4cdn.com](https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/DAL-12-31-2025-10K-2-10-26-Filed.pdf))

Minority interest is set to null because Delta’s filings here did not present a standalone 'noncontrolling interests' line item in the places accessed during this run; other equity stakes exist but are treated as investments rather than minority interests for this schema. ([s2.q4cdn.com](https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/DAL-12-31-2025-10K-2-10-26-Filed.pdf))

NOL balance uses Delta’s disclosed U.S. federal pre-tax net operating loss carryforwards amount (~$2.4B) and assumes 80% utilization (schema default). Actual utilization depends on taxable income generation and limitations/recognition. ([s2.q4cdn.com](https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/DAL-12-31-2025-10K-2-10-26-Filed.pdf))
Comps: NTM EV/Revenue and EV/EBITDA and NTM P/E were not available from consistent free sources in this run; comps numeric fields are set to null with an explanation.

catalysts: Sustained demand/pricing that supports revenue growth and operating leverage versus base-case margin trajectory. ([ir.delta.com](https://ir.delta.com/news/news-details/2026/Delta-Air-Lines-Announces-December-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx))

Fuel-cost volatility and hedging outcomes materially impacting operating income and free cash flow. ([s2.q4cdn.com](https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/DAL-12-31-2025-10K-2-10-26-Filed.pdf))
Execution of fleet/cost initiatives (including MRO separability detail and operational efficiency) that could shift EBIT margin above/below the path.
company_overview: Delta Air Lines operates a global passenger and cargo network and is a member of the SkyTeam airline alliance. ([s2.q4cdn.com](https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/DAL-12-31-2025-10K-2-10-26-Filed.pdf))

Delta’s customer proposition is reinforced by its SkyMiles loyalty program and a differentiated, premium-oriented product offering. ([s2.q4cdn.com](https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/DAL-12-31-2025-10K-2-10-26-Filed.pdf))

Delta also operates a refinery business (Monroe Energy / Trainer refinery) that supports jet fuel supply and generates refinery-related revenue. ([s2.q4cdn.com](https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/DAL-12-31-2025-10K-2-10-26-Filed.pdf))
current_context: Full-year 2025 (GAAP): operating revenue $63.4 billion; operating income $5.8 billion; operating margin 9.2%. ([ir.delta.com](https://ir.delta.com/news/news-details/2026/Delta-Air-Lines-Announces-December-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx))

Company outlook: 2026 earnings expected to grow 20% YoY and March-quarter 2026 revenue growth guided to 5%–7% YoY. ([ir.delta.com](https://ir.delta.com/news/news-details/2026/Delta-Air-Lines-Announces-December-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx))

2026 guidance bands: EPS $6.50–$7.50; 1Q26 EPS $0.50–$0.90; operating margin 4.5%–6%; free cash flow $3–$4 billion (company-provided ranges). ([ir.delta.com](https://ir.delta.com/news/news-details/2026/Delta-Air-Lines-Announces-December-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx))
investment_highlights: Base case reflects low-to-mid single digit revenue growth and gradual re-expansion/normalization of EBIT margin toward ~9.45% by 2030, consistent with management’s margin expansion framing. ([ir.delta.com](https://ir.delta.com/news/news-details/2026/Delta-Air-Lines-Announces-December-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx))

Depreciation and amortization is held around ~3.9% of sales to reflect a stable reinvestment/depreciation profile, aligned with recent history. ([s2.q4cdn.com](https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/DAL-12-31-2025-10K-2-10-26-Filed.pdf))

Capex intensity gradually declines from 2025’s level (reflecting a normalization after a lower 2025 cash capex print) toward ~7.3% of sales by 2030. ([s2.q4cdn.com](https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/DAL-12-31-2025-10K-2-10-26-Filed.pdf))

Working-capital is negative in the historical and forecast drivers, consistent with airlines’ large deferred/air-traffic liabilities; base-case NWC stays around -29% to -30% of sales. ([s2.q4cdn.com](https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/DAL-12-31-2025-10K-2-10-26-Filed.pdf))
key_risks: Macroeconomic downturn or demand shock causing unit revenue and margin underperformance versus modeled growth. ([ir.delta.com](https://ir.delta.com/news/news-details/2026/Delta-Air-Lines-Announces-December-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx))

Higher-than-modeled labor, airport, or disruption costs compressing operating margins. ([s2.q4cdn.com](https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/DAL-12-31-2025-10K-2-10-26-Filed.pdf))
Balance-sheet/liquidity constraints and capital market conditions affecting the effective cost of capital (WACC) used in the DCF.

valuation_summary: DCF build anchors on 2023–2025 actuals (revenue, operating income as EBIT, D&A, and cash capex derived from property/equipment additions). ([s2.q4cdn.com](https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/DAL-12-31-2025-10K-2-10-26-Filed.pdf))

Terminal value uses a Gordon growth approach with WACC ~8.4% and terminal growth 2.5%, targeting economically plausible long-run maturity for a developed-market airline. ([tradingeconomics.com](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/10-year-treasury-constant-maturity-rate-percent-d-na-fed-data.html))
